newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady despite firmer crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady despite firmer crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady on Thursday, despite crude's late rally.
Gasoline was steady and mostly balanced, traders said.
One dealer noted a shortage of high octane supply, and saw traders bringing supplies into the region from NWE at Rotterdam eurograde barges +$30 cif Med.
Naphtha was also steady, but paraffinic supply was still tight due to the continued closure of Algeria's Skikda port.
Gas oil prices were unchanged as slightly higher IPE futures were counteracted by an easing in premiums.
A cargo of heating oil was sold fob Med quotes +$2, down slightly from Wednesday's levels. A cargo of Russian heating oil was done at cif Med quotes +$1/1.25.
Algerian was offered at EN590 quotes cif Med +$3/3.50 but traders said this was too expensive. Much material was said to be heading north.
Traders with contracts to supply Greece with 600,000 tonnes of gas oil were seen bringing in vessels from Black Sea ports in the next few days.
Fuel oil was steady despite volatile crude.

A 50,000-tonne cargo was heard sold with October 23-25 loading dates amid talk it was destined for Romania and a cargo of low sulphur straight-run already in Augusta was sold at low cif quotes to an Italian buyer.
A M-40 was also sold at formula +$1.50-2.00.
Low sulphur was slow with continued talk of congestion in Italy thought to be hindering buying from the main Med buyer. Prices were steady around $135 cif Italy.
